analysis.title: Fed's Waller Backs 50bp hike / US CPI Ahead / Nvidia & China / Brent Below $90 / Iran & US
key_insights: Fed Governor Waller said he would support a 25bp December hike even if October inflation improves, and that a 50bp hike should be considered if core CPI rises 0.3% or more m/m. October CPI is due Tuesday, the last inflation reading before the Dec. 8-9 FOMC.
UBS economist Alan Detmeister forecasts October headline CPI at 0.26% m/m versus 0.29% consensus and a 0.32% UBS Nowcast, and core CPI at 0.23% versus 0.24% consensus and 0.22% Nowcast.

Waller called September's inflation data 'bad' and cited breadth of price increases, Fed staff analysis pointing to further producer-price pressures, and potentially more persistent effects from elevated energy prices.

Nvidia fell 5.5% on Monday on allegations around CEO Jensen Huang. The desk says most investors expect the issue to blow over, and there is little sign of investors backing away from a January-quarter revenue bogey closer to $135 bn.
The desk's best estimate is that Nvidia's China exposure is concentrated in a portion of Singapore revenue, where assemblers may be serving Chinese companies. Other geographies appear less connected.

Brent fell below $90 for the first time since August 31, about 23% below its $118 six-month high on Oct. 30. Trump said he would hold off on new strikes against Iran, OPEC output rose in October, and high prices have dampened demand.

Iran's security chief Rezaei called US reports of negotiations 'fake news' and demanded acceptance of seven conditions. Tehran says normal Hormuz traffic will not resume until they are met, though messages continue through mediators.
UBS Rates desk (Amar Mian) keeps a December Fed hike as base case with a more patient path in 2027. Preferred expressions are H7/H8 steepeners, receiving 2s5s30s and front-end spread wideners.

UBS equity research (Karl Keirstead) argues the market is too bearish on political risk to AI data-center capacity. The debate is more about permitting than stopping projects under construction, so the larger impact falls on 2028+ capacity.

CTA positioning is rotating out of tech and duration shorts into Europe and credit. Nasdaq momentum has flipped short, simulations show $40 bn of equity selling at 7,200 and positive flows only near 7,900, and CTAs have roughly halved US10y and EU10y shorts.
CTAs remain long USD and short most G10 and Asian currencies, with GBP and selected EM and Asian FX shorts expected to decline and AUD shorts to build. Energy is the strongest commodity pocket.

Riksbank raised its policy rate 25bp to 2.0% and expects further hikes over the coming year, citing a stronger economy, energy and producer prices, supply disruptions and a weaker krona. Aino Bunge favored a gradual approach.

Japan September household spending fell 6.8% y/y versus a consensus decline of 3.1%, the largest slide since September 2020. Some BoJ policymakers urged faster hikes, the BoJ is at 1.25%, and a December hike is widely expected.
UBS China Economics (Yu Song) expects GDP growth of about 4.6% in 2027, a growth target of 4.5-5%, a smaller net export contribution, stable soft consumption and further RMB appreciation.

UBS GBP rates desk sees the December/February MPC pricing of about 16.5bp as too low and favors payers into 16-22bp. It favors buying sub-3-year gilts and 7-10-year asset swaps after the MPC's 8-1 hawkish vote.
Australian Westpac consumer sentiment fell 2.7% to 78.2 in November, the lowest since late 2022, after the RBA's 25bp hike. Mortgage-holder sentiment hit a record low of 68.1.

UBS equity research (Timothy Arcuri) says the SOX's roughly 30% drop over the past month prices in about 30% and 35% cuts to Street CY2027 and CY2028 EPS, equal to about 55GW of CY2028 shipments versus an original 70GW. High-confidence powered-shell capacity is roughly 50GW.
UBS FX desk reports systematic and hedge fund USD selling on a positive risk tone, with EURUSD resistance at 1.1240 and 1.1280 and support at 1.1180/90 and 1.1100. US CPI is the next catalyst.
USDKRW fell from 1347.7 toward 1335 on heavy exporter selling, with a $63 bn September current account surplus. Next support levels are 1330 and 1320.
UBS Rates (Capuano) expects EUR benchmark covered bond issuance near EUR200 bn in 2027 with net supply of only EUR11 bn, and sees 5-10bp of spread widening in H1.

Arcuri: current SOX prices imply roughly 30% and 35% cuts to Street CY2027 and CY2028 EPS estimates (implied by market pricing, not a published estimate change).

risk_factors: A core CPI print of 0.3% m/m or more would put a 50bp December Fed hike on the table.
Nvidia allegations around CEO Jensen Huang remain unresolved, and the China shipment exposure is uncertain.
Political risk around data-center permitting could constrain AI capacity growth in 2027/28.
Iran has no clear near-term path to restoring normal Hormuz flows despite Trump's assessment.
Persistent energy and producer price pressures could keep inflation elevated.
Global fragmentation is raising the cost of capital for equity and credit.
Downside-skewed aggregate equity flows, with $40 bn of selling simulated at 7,200.
vol_and_positioning: CTAs: Nasdaq momentum flipped short and S&P momentum is deteriorating. Simulations show $40 bn of selling at 7,200 and positive flows only near 7,900.
CTAs have roughly halved US10y and EU10y short positions but remain broadly short, with further covering likely, especially in Japan, Australia and the EU long end.
CTAs remain long USD and short most G10 and Asian currencies, with AUD shorts building.
Credit liquidation is starting to reverse, with prospective buying led by European IG and HY.
Systematic and hedge fund accounts have been reducing long USD positions.
UBS vol strategy team call invited for Nov. 10 at 8:15 New York time.
geopolitical: Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei rejected US reports of negotiations, demanded acceptance of seven conditions conveyed via Qatar, and says normal Hormuz traffic will not resume until they are met.
Trump said he would hold off on new US strikes against Iran after appeals from regional countries.
The US naval blockade and frozen Iranian funds are among Iran's three publicly named demands.
Questions over Nvidia's relationship with Washington, including China access versus pressure for US domestic foundry investment.
French political uncertainty cited as a factor for EUR covered bond spreads.
Fragmentation of the global economy is cited as raising the cost of capital.

tension_points.bull_case: Keirstead says permitting changes target the approval process, not projects under construction, with the bigger impact on 2028+ capacity. Tighter permitting could also reduce capex and credit risk and raise the scarcity value of existing sites.
tension_points.bear_case: Keirstead does not fully buy the scarcity argument and views any constraint on AI capacity as ultimately negative for the ecosystem.

tension_points.bull_case: Most conversations expect the issue to blow over, and the earnings bar of about $135 bn for the January quarter looks intact.
tension_points.bear_case: If the issue persists, attention turns to management depth, and the relationship with the US government and China shipments remain open questions.
